analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md, a documentation file with no executable code. It bumps the 'Last updated' date at line 3. It also adds statements to the load_model, prefetch_model and desired_models sections (head lines ~1412-1414, 1422-1424, 1456-1464). Per the patch excerpt, those statements say a provider without saved Autopilot consent refuses a model outside the operator filter with model_not_selected. For prefetch_model the refusal comes before any download. For desired_models the patch excerpt is truncated, so the exact text about operator-filter behavior is not visible.

Security relevance: this describes a provider-side restriction that narrows coordinator-driven model load/download. It is a tightening of the described trust boundary (TB-002), where the coordinator is trusted but commands are validated by the provider. It introduces no new attack surface. It does not weaken the existing Autopilot model_not_selected allowlist checks (ModelAutopilotPolicy.rejection), the legacy lifecycle, or any App Attest controls in TB-011 and T-053 through T-058.

I examined base units 6 and 7 (base text lines 1287-1720) and head unit 8 (head text lines 1-316). The head text of the changed regions beyond line 316 is not supplied, so the 1412-1464 head edits are seen only through the patch excerpt. The actual enforcement in provider code (autopilotAllowsModel, the operator filter in configuration.md) is outside the supplied evidence. The documentation claims should be checked against that source in any pass that covers the Swift provider code. This is a documentation-accuracy question, not a finding. I identified no concrete security regression.
